diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), not otherwise specified (NOS), non-germinal-center B-cell-like (non-GCB) by the Hans algorithm, with a double-expressor immunophenotype (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%), stage III (Ann Arbor/Lugano IIIS), IPI 2. Relevant history: left breast invasive ductal carcinoma (2016; pT2 pN0, ER-positive/HER2-negative) in remission on anastrozole. The left axillary biopsy shows no evidence of metastatic breast carcinoma (cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and GATA3 negative in the lesional cells).
stage: Stage III (Ann Arbor/Lugano IIIS): FDG-avid lymphadenopathy above the diaphragm (left axillary, mediastinal) and below the diaphragm (mesenteric conglomerate 7.5 cm, para-aortic), with multifocal splenic involvement. There is no extralymphatic organ involvement (liver, lung, bone, adrenal, and kidney are negative), the bone marrow biopsy is negative, and there are no CNS symptoms. The spleen is a lymphatic organ, so splenic involvement is stage III (IIIS), not stage IV. IPI 2 (low-intermediate); age-adjusted IPI 2; NCCN-IPI 3 (low-intermediate); CNS-IPI 2 (intermediate).
biology: DLBCL, NOS, non-GCB (CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1 positive), double-expressor by immunohistochemistry (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%) with high proliferation (Ki-67 80%) and focal necrosis. Interphase FISH is negative for MYC, BCL2, and BCL6 rearrangements, so this is not a double-hit or triple-hit high-grade B-cell lymphoma. EBER is negative; CD5, CD30, and cyclin D1 are negative; cytokeratin and GATA3 are negative, excluding metastatic breast carcinoma. This is an aggressive but potentially curable B-cell lymphoma. The double-expressor phenotype is associated with inferior outcomes after R-CHOP, but there is no established standard targeted escalation outside a clinical trial.
prognosis: Potentially curable with curative-intent immunochemotherapy. The IPI is 2 (low-intermediate), but adverse features include the double-expressor phenotype, Ki-67 80%, LDH 510 U/L (about 2.3 times the upper limit of normal), a 7.5 cm mesenteric mass, splenic involvement, and B symptoms (fevers and night sweats). Expected 5-year PFS/OS is on the order of 60-70%, with the double-expressor phenotype and the need for an anthracycline-free regimen adding uncertainty. CNS relapse risk is intermediate (CNS-IPI 2) with no high-risk extranodal site, so I do not recommend routine CNS prophylaxis.
first_line_treatment: Curative-intent anthracycline-free immunochemotherapy: R-CEOP every 21 days for 6 cycles (rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV day 1; cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 IV day 1; etoposide 50 mg/m2 IV days 1-3; vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 IV day 1, capped at 2 mg; prednisone 100 mg PO days 1-5), with pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC on day 2. The decision is driven by the baseline LVEF 45% with reduced global longitudinal strain, prior cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, prior left breast radiotherapy, and hypertension; additional anthracycline would carry a high risk of further cardiac dysfunction and heart failure. I am not using R-CHOP or pola-R-CHP because both contain doxorubicin. If cardio-oncology confirms that the cardiac risk is acceptable and the patient, after informed discussion, prefers an anthracycline-based approach, I would use R-CHOP with dexrazoxane rather than R-CHOP alone. No consolidative radiotherapy is planned unless the end-of-treatment PET shows residual localized disease.
cns_risk: CNS-IPI 2 (intermediate risk; points for stage III and elevated LDH; age under 60, ECOG 1, no more than one extranodal site, and no kidney or adrenal involvement). There is no high-risk site (no breast parenchymal, adrenal, renal, bone marrow, or epidural involvement), and the lymphoma is not double-hit. I do not recommend intrathecal methotrexate or high-dose IV methotrexate prophylaxis. I will monitor clinically for neurologic symptoms and perform CSF evaluation only if symptoms or radiologic CNS disease develop.
response_assessment: I will not use routine interim PET to change therapy outside a clinical trial. Response will be assessed with a whole-body FDG PET-CT about 6-8 weeks after cycle 6, interpreted by Lugano/Deauville criteria (Deauville 1-3 = complete metabolic response; Deauville 4-5 = residual disease, with biopsy of a residual FDG-avid site if it would change management). I will also repeat echocardiography with GLS at the end of therapy because of the baseline LVEF 45%. If there is a complete metabolic response, proceed to surveillance with history and physical examination every 3-6 months for 2 years and then less frequently, without routine surveillance PET. If there is a partial response or progression, biopsy and move to second-line platinum-based salvage therapy, with evaluation for CAR-T or autologous transplant if eligible.
pretreatment_workup: Already completed: excisional left axillary lymph node biopsy with immunohistochemistry, flow cytometry, and FISH; staging FDG PET-CT; bone marrow aspirate and biopsy (negative); CBC with differential, comprehensive metabolic panel, LDH, uric acid, and beta-2 microglobulin; HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs, HCV antibody, and HIV antigen/antibody; transthoracic echocardiogram with GLS; ECOG status; and a full history and physical. Before cycle 1: formal cardio-oncology consultation and confirmation of LVEF/GLS (repeat echocardiogram or cardiac MRI if there is uncertainty); repeat CBC, CMP, LDH, and uric acid; baseline neurologic examination for vincristine; dental evaluation; blood pressure optimization; expert hematopathology review; and documentation of hepatitis B vaccination status (anti-HBs is negative). A pregnancy test is not needed. Lumbar puncture/CSF evaluation is not indicated without neurologic symptoms. No routine GI endoscopy or PJP prophylaxis is needed.
supportive_care: Tumor lysis syndrome: allopurinol 300 mg daily (adjust for renal function) with vigorous hydration starting before cycle 1 and close monitoring of uric acid, creatinine, potassium, phosphorus, and calcium; because of the 7.5 cm mass and LDH 510 U/L, I will monitor closely and use rasburicase if uric acid rises or renal function declines. Growth factor: pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC on day 2 (or filgrastim) with each cycle. Antiemetics: a 5-HT3 antagonist plus dexamethasone, with an NK1 antagonist if needed for the etoposide-containing regimen. Infection: no HBV antiviral prophylaxis is needed because HBsAg and anti-HBc are negative; anti-HBs is negative, so arrange hepatitis B vaccination; give inactivated influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal, and recombinant zoster vaccines as appropriate, and avoid live vaccines during immunosuppression. No routine PJP prophylaxis with this regimen unless corticosteroids are prolonged. Cardiac: cardio-oncology co-management, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB and a beta-blocker for LVEF 45% if not contraindicated, optimize blood pressure, monitor for dyspnea or edema, and repeat echocardiography with GLS at the end of therapy. Continue anastrozole 1 mg daily without interruption; it is not myelosuppressive and has no clinically significant interaction with R-CEOP, and stopping it would increase breast cancer recurrence risk. Continue calcium and vitamin D for osteopenia. Use a bowel regimen with vincristine and monitor for peripheral neuropathy. No routine VTE prophylaxis in the ambulatory setting. Provide psychosocial support, work accommodations, and transportation planning.
fitness_and_goals: ECOG 1, age 59, independent, working full-time, with good social support from her husband; she is fit for full-dose curative-intent immunochemotherapy. The main limitation is cardiac reserve, not performance status or frailty. Her stated goal is cure and return to full-time work, and she is anxious about heart failure because of her mother's history. I recommend a shared decision with cardio-oncology that favors an anthracycline-free regimen (R-CEOP) to protect the heart while maintaining curative intent. If she develops symptomatic heart failure or the LVEF falls below 40%, I would reassess and further modify therapy. If she were to decline intensive chemotherapy, R-miniCHOP or a palliative approach would be considered, but she is not in that category. I will also coordinate with breast oncology about completing anastrozole in November 2026.
missing_information: Formal cardio-oncology assessment, including a repeat echocardiogram with GLS (or cardiac MRI if there is uncertainty), to confirm LVEF 45% and to advise on anthracycline avoidance versus dexrazoxane use.
Expert hematopathology review to confirm DLBCL, NOS versus high-grade B-cell lymphoma and to verify the MYC/BCL2 double-expressor scoring and FISH results.
TP53 mutation and gene-expression cell-of-origin status (prognostic only; not required for standard first-line treatment).
Baseline peripheral neuropathy assessment and documentation of any pre-existing vincristine risk factors.
Hepatitis B vaccination plan because anti-HBs is negative, and confirmation of prior vaccination status.
The patient's informed preference about the trade-off between cardiac risk and intensity of lymphoma therapy, and whether she wishes to consider a clinical trial.
Local availability and access to R-CEOP versus liposomal doxorubicin and dexrazoxane.
The exact cardiac radiation dose from the prior left breast radiotherapy, which would refine the cardiotoxicity risk estimate.
Baseline dental evaluation before starting chemotherapy.
No CSF cytology or CNS imaging has been obtained; this is appropriate absent neurologic symptoms, but would be obtained if symptoms develop.
